text:
The evidence can't confirm that timber harvest caused the loss.

What it does show: about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 (2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha asset). The loss is corroborated. A later year was observed, and the 2020 JRC forest map agrees over 98% of the event area. The national forest map classes 68.1 ha of the event area as planted pine (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha as outside mapped forest, and none as native forest. A further 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

The planted-forest context makes harvest plausible, but the tool states that this context describes the territory and is never the cause. Hansen loss captures any stand replacement, including cutting a plantation, but also fire, storms or clearing. The output explicitly does not establish cause, legality, actor, or deforestation or compliance status.

To attribute the cause, you would need harvest records, management plans or permits, or imagery and field evidence of operations.
